prompts.task: Create ./service/.observe and copy the four canonical JSON inputs from ./service/eval/inputs into their standard .observe names. Render .observe/otel.html once, record its SHA-256, and run $otel-verify read-only against the bound AO-003 dependency closure. Reconcile ao-gateway-verify-evidence.txt with source and the supplied proof packet, then validate the complete audit -> selection -> instrumentation -> verify flow. Keep the two synthetic projectid/logstreamid pairs isolated, but do not represent their UUIDs as real cloud resources. The recorded loopback HTTP 202 acknowledgments prove only the local route contract; they do not prove app.py ran, cloud forwarding, or fresh cloud Agent Stream visibility. Preserve the audit HTML bytes while refreshing verification JSON, reader-first Markdown, and instrumentation HTML. If a live cloud query or application execution is unavailable, keep those outcomes Not proven and report the exact missing proof rather than inventing cloud results. Do not edit app.py or add instrumentation. Assess the supplied packet against this additional recovery acceptance: The audit-selected project and dedicated Agent Stream names already exist, but the application initially has names only and Studio may be disconnected. No UUIDs are prefilled. The same running process must eventually resolve/reuse the exact scoped resources when the configured API becomes available, with zero creates, no manual setup command and no restart. Preserve any previously resolved complete binding across a transient 503 for the same destination. Native OTel requires matching projectid/logstreamid headers and splunk_ao.project.id/splunk_ao.logstream.id trace Resource attributes; preserve SDK-owned routing and metric/log Resources. The packet does not prove same-PID recovery or native trace Resource metadata; keep those outcomes explicitly unproven rather than adding code or deriving them from the two header pairs.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service/.observe/otel-audit.json, otel-selection.json, otel-instrumentation.json, otel-verify.json, otel.html, otel-verify.md, and otel-instrumentation.html.
rubric: Checks AO configuration independently of ordinary OTLP configuration and evaluates the selected mode without rewriting endpoints or adding profiles. Recognizes that no Studio-only profile, installed-SDK mode-isolation check, or resource-before-export/failure test is supplied by this proof packet; reports those missing configuration/runtime checks accurately rather than deriving AO compatibility from OTLP receipt or claiming the synthetic IDs were resolved resources.

Uses the existing canonical AI-assistant AO audit without modifying its bytes or digest, validates the exact AO-003 selection closure in audit order, and binds verification to the normalized instrumentation overlay rather than matching IDs alone.

Checks both synthetic local requests retain their distinct projectid/logstreamid pairs, with no cross-stream leakage or invented global AO destination. Treats those UUIDs only as route-test values, not as proof that real cloud project and Agent Stream resources exist.

Reports HTTP 202 as local gateway or receiver acknowledgment only. Does not equate local receipt, SDK resource response, upstream ingest acknowledgment, or ordinary APM visibility with a fresh trace visible in the intended cloud Agent Stream. AO project, dedicated stream, live app routing, and cloud Agent Stream delivery remain Not proven absent direct evidence; the overall result cannot be Pass on this evidence alone.

Keeps application code and dependencies unchanged in this read-only verification task. Any source/config or synthetic-contract checks retain their honest proof mode and durable evidence rather than being promoted to full application runtime proof.

Writes bound canonical verification JSON and reader-first .observe/otel-verify.md with precise What Changed, Tested And Working, Not Working Or Not Proven, and Proof outcomes; refreshes .observe/otel-instrumentation.html while preserving .observe/otel.html byte-for-byte and retaining its selected AO subsection state.

Recognizes that synthetic header receipts do not prove names-only same-PID recovery, exact existing-resource reuse without creates, or matching native trace Resource fields. Reports those distinct outcomes Not proven on this packet. Does not present seeded IDs, restart-based tests, transient-503 header stripping, or an env-file-only update as proof of runtime recovery. Keeps read-only application scope and exact cloud-readback requirements.
